arxiv-2109-07403.title: BERT is Robust! A Case Against Synonym-Based Adversarial Examples in Text Classification
arxiv-2109-07403.creator: Jens Hauser, Zhao Meng, Damián Pascual, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2109-07403.description: Abstract Deep Neural Networks have taken Natural Language Processing by storm. While this led to incredible improvements across many tasks, it also initiated a new research field, questioning the robustness of these neural networks by attacking them. In this paper, we investigate four word substitution-based attacks on BERT.

arxiv-2111-04841.title: First equilibrium reconstruction for ITER with the code NICE
arxiv-2111-04841.creator: C. Boulbe
arxiv-2111-04841.description: Abstract In this short paper we present the first application of the IMAS compatible code NICE to equilibrium reconstrution for ITER geometry. The inverse problem is formulated as a least square problem and the numerical methods implemented in NICE in order to solve it are presented.

arxiv-2308-00346.title: Dynamic ensemble selection based on Deep Neural Network Uncertainty Estimation for Adversarial Robustness
arxiv-2308-00346.creator: Ruoxi Qin, Linyuan Wang, Xuehui Du, Jian Chen, Xingyuan Chen, Bin Yan
arxiv-2308-00346.description: Abstract The deep neural network has attained significant efficiency in image recognition. However, it has vulnerable recognition robustness under extensive data uncertainty in practical applications. The uncertainty is attributed to the inevitable ambient noise and, more importantly, the possible adversarial attack. Dynamic methods can effectively improve the defense initiative in the arms race of attack and defense of adversarial examples.

arxiv-2403-19469.title: Dynamic interaction between chiral currents and surface waves in topological superfluids: a pathway to detect Majorana fermions?
arxiv-2403-19469.creator: S. Forstner 1,2, H. Choi 3,4, G.I. Harris 1, A. Sawadsky 1, W.P. Bowen 1, C.G. Baker 1
arxiv-2403-19469.description: Abstract Despite extensive experimental efforts over the past two decades, the quest for Majorana fermions in superconductors remains inconclusive. We propose an experimental method that can conclusively confirm, or rule out, the existence of these quasiparticles: Firstly, we shift focus from superconductors , whose very topological nature is disputed, to the unambiguous topological superfluid 3 He.

arxiv-2501-00899.title: Astrophysical Black holes: An Explanation for the Galaxy Quenching
arxiv-2501-00899.creator: Jay Verma Trivedi, Pankaj S. Joshi, Gopal-Krishna, Peter L. Biermann
arxiv-2501-00899.description: Abstract We propose models of Astrophysical Black holes (ABHs) without event horizons (EHs), as a more viable explanation for the long-term quenching phenomenon in galaxies. At the same time, the short-term quenching is explained here in terms of an efficient feedback expected in the models of stellar-mass astrophysical black holes (StMABHs).

arxiv-2505-12698.title: A Deep Learning Potential for Accurate Shock Response Simulations in Tin
arxiv-2505-12698.creator: Yixin Chen, Xiaoyang Wang, Wanghui Li, Mohan Chen, Han Wang
arxiv-2505-12698.description: Abstract Tin (Sn) plays a crucial role in studying the dynamic mechanical responses of ductile metals under shock loading. Atomistic simulations serves to unveil the nano-scale mechanisms for critical behaviors of dynamic responses. However, existing empirical potentials for Sn often lack sufficient accuracy when applied in such simulation.

arxiv-2508-03846.title: Empathy Guidelines for Improving Practitioner Well-being & Software Engineering Practices Journal: IEEE Software
arxiv-2508-03846.creator: Hashini Gunatilake, John Grundy, Rashina Hoda, Ingo Mueller
arxiv-2508-03846.description: Abstract Empathy is a powerful yet often overlooked element in software engineering (SE), supporting better teamwork, smoother communication, and effective decision-making. In our previous study, we identified a range of practitioner strategies for fostering empathy in SE contexts. Building on these insights, this paper introduces 17 actionable empathy guidelines designed to support practitioners, teams, and organisations.

arxiv-2509-22042.title: Entropy rates in the dimension theory of self-similar measures
arxiv-2509-22042.creator: Péter P. Varjú
arxiv-2509-22042.description: Abstract . This is a survey paper on the dimension theory of self-similar measures focusing on the role of entropy rates. 1. Introduction A (self-similar) iterated function system, IFS for short, is a finite collection \Phi=\{\varphi_{i}:i\in\Lambda\} of contractive similarities of {\mathbf{R}} . A contractive similarity is a map x\mapsto\lambda x+\tau , where \lambda\in(-1,1)\backslash\{0\} , \tau\in{\mathbf{R}} .

arxiv-2601-02465.title: GeV-scale QCD Axion
arxiv-2601-02465.creator: Hitoshi Murayama
arxiv-2601-02465.description: Abstract In order to solve the strong CP problem, we study the possibility that the Peccei–Quinn symmetry is broken below the QCD scale. We find that a QCD axion can be above GeV, and may be among the observed η \eta resonances. It is immune to quantum gravity corrections.

pmc-10626394.title: Thermal, photonic, and electrocatalysis in lignin depolymerization research
pmc-10626394.creator: Wang Ziwei, Shu Hao, Chen Yizhen, Liu Ben, Xu Yaowei, Wang Wanxia, Wang Kaiyue, Lei Mengheng, Guo Li, Wang Lei
pmc-10626394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In order to realize a sustainable bio-based future, it is essential to fully harness the potential of biomass, including lignin – a readily available biopolymer that ranks second in abundance and serves as a renewable source of aromatics. While lignin has traditionally been used for lower-value applications like fuel and power generation, unlocking its higher-value potential through diverse conversion and upgrading techniques is of paramount importance.

pmc-11709917.title: TRIDENT cognitive substudy: preliminary results from a Brazilian cohort
pmc-11709917.creator: Ana Cláudia de Souza, Wyllians Vendramini Borelli, Kendi Nishino Miyamoto, Ana Claudia Alves, Mariana Almudi, Adriana Binsfeld Hess, Renata Kochhann, Leonardo Augusto Carbonera, Sheila O Martins, Craig S. Anderson

High rates of cognitive decline and dementia follow acute ICH, due to the common underlying vasculopathy of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD).

pmc-13149966.title: NANP targeting radiosensitizes glioblastoma through TNFR1 sialylation-driven mesenchymal shift
pmc-13149966.creator: Yingwen Ding, Ze-Yan Zhang, Ravesanker Ezhilarasan, Aram S. Modrek, Melanie Graciani, Jerome Karp, Graysen McManus, Ananya Jambhale, Erik P. Sulman
pmc-13149966.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) patients have dismal survival due to resistance to initial ionizing radiation therapy (RT). Clonal evolution analysis reveals no dominant RT-resistant clones, prompting a genome-wide CRISPR screen to identify radiosensitizing targets. The screening highlights DNA damage response genes, validating the effectiveness of our approach.

pmc-13167214.title: Frontal ataxia: a frequent but underrecognized disorder in the spectrum of ataxias
pmc-13167214.creator: Beatriz Cassarotti, Patrícia Aurea Andreucci Martins Bonilha, Thabata Emanuelle Martins Nunes, Léo Coutinho, Carlos Henrique Ferreira Camargo, Hélio Afonso Ghizoni Teive
pmc-13167214.description: BackgroundAtaxia comprises a heterogeneous group of disorders with multiple clinical and etiological presentations. The frontal subtype, in particular, is poorly defined and often misdiagnosed, reflecting both its complex historical evolution and lack of formal diagnostic criteria.ObjectiveTo evaluate clinical and epidemiological characteristics of a sample of patients with ataxia under follow-up in a private neurology clinic.

pmc-13278905.title: Predictive modeling for cervical cancer: existing AI approaches and the emerging role of vaginal microbiome
pmc-13278905.creator: Michelle Gomes, Zonglun Li, Adeola Olaitan, Aleksandra Gentry-Maharaj
pmc-13278905.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, yet current screening tools lack precision in identifying which women with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection will progress to high-grade lesions or cancer. Within a network-physiology framework, cervical carcinogenesis is viewed as emerging from dynamic interactions between viral dynamics, host immunity, vaginal ecology, vaccination status and behaviour rather than from isolated risk factors.

pmc-13299690.title: Omsk Hemorrhagic Fever Virus and Powassan Virus Infections at Different Times After Immunization with the TBE Vaccine in In Vivo Experiments
pmc-13299690.creator: Viktoria Kuchina, Ksenia Tuchynskaya, Anastasia Rogova, Galina Karganova
pmc-13299690.description: Ranges of distribution of some orthoflaviviruses, including the Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus (OHFV) and the Powassan virus (POWV), have been identified in the range endemic for the tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV). In contrast to TBEV, no registered vaccine against OHFV and POWV is currently available.

pmc-13330252.title: Depression, anxiety and stress among nursing students: a latent profile analysis
pmc-13330252.creator: Li Zeng, Jiayi Zhou, Yuan Zhang, Zhongqing Yuan, Fengxue Yang, Xiuying Hu
pmc-13330252.description: BackgroundNursing students experience high prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress, but traditional variable‑centered approaches may overlook distinct subgroups. This study aimed to identify homogeneous profiles of affective distress and examine their related factors.MethodsNursing students (n = 1184) from five medical colleges in Sichuan Province, China were recruited from March 3 to May 30, 2025.

pmc-13549751.title: Real-world survey of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in Japan using a nationwide administrative claims database
pmc-13549751.creator: Yachiyo Kuwatsuka, Kikue Sato, Yoshiko Atsuta, Tetsuya Nishida, Yukiyasu Ozawa, Masayuki Hino, Koichi Miyamura
pmc-13549751.description: According to data from the Japanese registry managed by the Transplant Registry Unified Management Program, the number of autologous stem cell transplantations (auto-SCT) in 2018 was approximately 60% of that of allogeneic SCT (allo-SCT). The opposite trend has been reported in the United States. Thus, we hypothesized that auto-SCT is underreported in the registry.
